newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Vice President Joseph Estrada challenges President Fidel Ramos to a one-on-one fight in next year's elections. (MANILA CHRONICLE)
- House speaker Jose de Venecia says he has dropped the bill to allow people's initiative to amend the Constitution from his priority list. (TODAY)
- The management of Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System calls for an emergency meeting as the labour crisis in the water service agency enters its second day (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Presidential Commission Against Graft and Corruption discloses that senators and congressmen have appropriated a total of 5.63 billion pesos to their affiliate offices between 1993 and 1995 (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Philippine peso came under attack after the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht. Turnover hit an all-time high of $1.049 billion. (ALL PAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos says the International Monetary Fund mission believes the Philippine economy is sound but lacked some legislative changes. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Garments and textiles exports rise by eight percent in the first half of the year, the Garments and Textiles Export Board says. (TODAY)

- Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo says the consolidated public sector generated a surplus of 541 million pesos in the first half of the year, better than the 5.7 billion deficit targetted for the period. (ALL PAPERS)
